researched.reason: Aeroflex Enterprises Ltd, market cap Rs 1,527.2 cr, close Rs 134.95. Its own Reg 30 filing of 14-Oct-2026 reports that Aeroflex Industries Ltd - its 65.47%-owned, separately listed subsidiary - approved Rs 202 cr of capacity expansion: SS hose and braiding from 20 to 30 million metres p.a. plus a new assemblies plant to convert 70-75% of hoses into assemblies (Rs 124 cr), and liquid-cooling SFN skid assemblies from 15,000 to 30,000 pieces p.a. (Rs 78 cr), phased to March 2028, funded by equity, bridge loan and internal accruals. The subsidiary's own press release the same day states the expanded capacity should generate INCREMENTAL REVENUE OF Rs 500-550 CR at peak utilisation - that is +121% to +133% of its FY26 revenue of Rs 412.47 cr, an implied incremental asset turn of 2.5-2.7x. What made this publishable rather than another press release is that the physical driver is disclosed quarter by quarter in the subsidiary's own filings: skid capacity 2,000 pieces p.a. (Dec-2025) to 6,000 (01-Apr-2026, with 571 units sold in Q4 FY26) to 9,000 (01-Jul-2026, with 1,040 units sold in Q1 FY27) to 12,000 complete now, and the units sold almost doubled quarter on quarter at about 46% utilisation. The subsidiary's results corroborate it: Q1 FY27 revenue Rs 139.01 cr (+75.5% YoY) and PAT Rs 19.06 cr (+150.1%). Exposure for the holding company is documented twice over - its own filing calls Aeroflex Industries its material subsidiary, and the subsidiary's June-2026 shareholding pattern shows promoter holding of 65.47%. Look-through, from market caps read out of this run's BSE scrip master: 65.47% of Rs 7,528.3 cr plus 55.50% of Aeroflex Neu's Rs 179.9 cr is Rs 5,027.6 cr of listed value against the holdco's own Rs 1,527.2 cr - it trades at 30.4%, a 69.6% discount. Promoter holding in the holdco is RISING (51.59% Mar-2026, 52.30% Jun-2026, 52.45% Sep-2026) with repeated SAST Reg 29(2) filings by A Flex Invest. Published at CONFIDENCE LOW, and the reason is stated on the card: the operating subsidiary is already at 112.9x trailing earnings after a +235.9% year, so the expansion is largely in its price, and no document read this run names any catalyst - demerger, buyback, open offer, dividend - that would narrow the holdco discount. Holdco EPS could not be modelled because the equity portion of the Rs 202 cr is unquantified. The order study was not invoked: this is a capex, not an order.

Bajaj Healthcare Ltd, market cap Rs 1,116 cr, the day's third-highest candidate. The trigger filing was opened in full, including its Form A annexure: the NCLT Mumbai Bench, by order dated 13-Oct-2026, APPROVED the acquisition of Genrx Pharmaceuticals Private Limited (in Liquidation) on a going-concern basis, making Genrx a wholly owned subsidiary. NOT PUBLISHED, on three measured grounds. First, the filing carries NO financial number at all - item 7, 'expected financial implications', says only that Genrx will become a wholly owned subsidiary. Second, the deal's size was found by going back to the original disclosure of 05-Apr-2025, which states a cash consideration of Rs 10,85,00,000 for 100% control: Rs 10.85 cr is 0.97% of market cap, and the triage rules skip triggers with no material number. Third, and decisive, that same 2025 annexure answers 'history of last 3 years turnover' with 'Company was in liquidation since 2020' - Genrx has NO revenue history. So what was acquired is pharmaceutical formulation manufacturing FACILITIES, with no disclosed capacity, no stated revenue potential and no management guidance attached, and today's filing is the judicial completion of an 18-month-old deal rather than a new operational trigger. Nothing here supports a physical revenue model, which is what this page publishes.
